text:
olivia: Quick sync — we need a concrete plan for AWS KMS integration for Redwood Private (VPC) control-plane + data-plane. Focus: envelope flow, cross-account/BYOK, rotation, audit signals, and emergency fallback. Who can take lead?

mike: I can drive the KMS auth model. Confirming: we want the CMK in the customer account (BYOK) and Redwood services assume role to call KMS, right?

olivia: Yes — primary pattern is customer-managed CMK in their account. We also need an option for customer-provided key material (imported key) and fallback to Redwood-managed CMK for onboarding.

tara: For low-latency dataplane ops, prefer using short-lived KMS grants instead of repeated `Encrypt`/`Decrypt` IAM checks. Grants avoid extra STS calls. We'll create a grant per service principal with limited ops (Encrypt, Decrypt, ReEncryptFrom, ReDecrypt). :white_check_mark:

mike: Agreed. High level envelope flow proposal: 1) service generates DEK locally (AES-256), 2) call `Encrypt` with CMK to produce EDEK, store EDEK with object metadata, 3) use DEK for symmetric ops, 4) on read, call `Decrypt` to unwrap DEK. Rotation = re-encrypt DEKs with new CMK (ReEncrypt).

olivia: Add control-plane nuance: control-plane handles secrets for routing and config (short-lived tokens). dataplane handles cached embeddings and model caches — both need DEK envelope but we should separate key usage by intent with key aliases or separate CMKs.

james: Quick IAM/trust snippet for role assumption (customer account -> redwood service role):

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::REDCUSTOMER:role/RedwoodControlplaneRole"},
      "Action": "sts:AssumeRole",
      "Condition": {}
    }
  ]
}
```

mike: KMS key policy minimal binding — allow the account root + the controlplane role to use key. Use explicit `kms:ViaService` if we want to restrict calls from specific VPC endpoints. Also ensure `kms:EncryptionContext` enforcement for tenant scoping.

tara: Example encryption-context check in key policy: "kms:EncryptionContext:tenant-id": "${aws:userid}" (or better: explicit value from control plane). We should validate context on decrypt.

olivia: Rotation playbook draft: 1) create new CMK in customer account (or enable AWS automatic rotation if acceptable), 2) run bulk `ReEncrypt` of all stored EDEKs to new CMK (use `ReEncrypt` or `ReEncryptFrom` to avoid plaintext export), 3) update alias to point to new key (alias swap after rewrap), 4) monitor for `AccessDenied` spikes, 5) schedule key deprecation window -> disable old key -> schedule deletion only after confirmation.

mike: CLI rewrap example (safe path):

```bash
aws kms re-encrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://edek.bin --destination-key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/new-key-id --source-encryption-context 'tenant=123' --destination-encryption-context 'tenant=123' > edek_new.bin
```

james: Audit logging checklist: - enable CloudTrail data events for KMS (Log all KMS API calls) - forward to central logging account with S3 bucket + lifecycle - set metric filter for `Decrypt`, `ReEncrypt`, `GenerateDataKey*` and alert on unusual spikes or calls outside expected regions/accounts. Also record `kms:RequestAlias` and `awsAccountId` in logs.

tara: Also create a CloudWatch Logs Insights query for quick triage, e.g.:

```
fields @timestamp, eventName, userIdentity.arn, requestParameters.ciphertextBlob
| filter eventName in ["Decrypt","ReEncrypt"]
| stats count() by userIdentity.arn, eventName
| sort @timestamp desc
```

olivia: RBAC changes we need in Redwood: - map customer roles to internal service roles (control-plane vs dataplane) - scope policies to `kms:EncryptionContext` tenant-id - restrict rewrap/rotate operations to a small ops group + automation role with MFA in account (or cross-account session constrained by `aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent`).

mike: For BYOK with imported key material, note: imported keys can't be backed up by AWS; rotation is limited. Recommend import only for regulated customers; prefer CMKs with customer-managed schedules. We should document limitations in onboarding checklist.

james: Incident response (key compromise) short playbook: 1) revoke active KMS grants for the CMK (`RevokeGrant`), 2) disable CMK (set key state to Disabled) to stop new decrypts, 3) bring up emergency Redwood-managed fallback CMK and rewrap DEKs to fallback key if we can access plaintext (if not, contact customer), 4) coordinate with customer to rotate to new CMK and rewrap. Post-incident: forensic review from CloudTrail + S3 access logs.

tara: Edge case: long-lived cached DEKs on worker hosts — ensure periodic in-memory zeroization and set DEK TTL so rewrap/rotation invalidates stale caches quickly. Keep TTL short for high-risk tenants.

olivia: Testing plan: unit tests for Encrypt/Decrypt, integration test that simulates rewrap (using `ReEncrypt`) and verifies `Decrypt` fails with old key after disable, chaos test: simulate lost cross-account trust (remove assume-role) and verify failover to Redwood-managed fallback path (and alerting flow).

mike: Ops automation: create a `kms-rewrap` job that runs in batches (idempotent), tracks progress via DynamoDB (or job-store), and emits events to Slack. Use exponential backoff for throttled ReEncrypt calls.

eng-kms-bot: checklist-run: kms-priv-design-v1 -> PASS: grants recommended, audit hooks present, rewrap workflow sketched. Next action: create RFC + runbook PR. :rocket:

olivia: Thanks — mike, please open RFC with proposed IAM snippets, grant lifecycle, and sample rewrap job by EOD Wednesday. I'll coordinate compliance sign-off and test plan.

mike: On it. I'll ping infra for quota guidance and ask infra to run a permission smoke test in staging.

james: I'll add CloudTrail/Alerts dashboard proto to the doc.

olivia: Awesome — leaving notes here for IR and onboarding docs. Will follow up with a short demo after RFC review. :slightly_smiling_face:
